Definition: of Latin origin; "custody", i.e. a Roman sentry:--watch.
BiblicalUsage: The word is a Latin loanword, custodia, a Roman guard, and all three appearances belong to the guard at Jesus' tomb. Pilate grants the watch in Matthew 27:65, the chief priests set it in Matthew 27:66, and in Matthew 28:11 some of the watch report to the chief priests what happened at the resurrection.
TheologicalSignificance: I am sure this guard is the proof of the resurrection's enemies: they did everything they could to keep the tomb shut, and it did not hold.
